concept.title: Project access (members)
concept.shortdesc: Project membership is managed in Settings → Access inside the project:

ul.li:
Add a member by email. Someone who already has an OpenV account joins straight away. Someone who has none is invited: OpenV emails them an invitation to the workspace that also opens this project, at the role you chose, and they join both when they accept it (see Inviting someone who has no account yet in Workspace settings & teams).
Inviting someone new brings them into the workspace and takes a seat there, so only a workspace admin can do it. A project owner who is not one is asked to have an admin invite the person first.
Invite them as an editor, reviewer or viewer; make them an owner once they have joined.
Someone who already has an invitation to the workspace keeps it, and it opens this project too; a pending admin invitation stays an admin one.
If the server has no email set up, the invitation link is shown once under the form for you to send.
On a workspace on the stable channel this arrives with its next stable release; until then an address with no account is refused, with a message asking them to sign up first.

Each member has a role — viewer, reviewer, editor, or owner (the add form defaults to editor; whoever creates a project becomes its owner) — you can change it from the members table, and members can be removed. A reviewer reads everything a viewer reads and adds notes, comments and mentions, but cannot change the text, the links, a status or a setting.

Team access grants a whole workspace team access to the project at once, with a role per grant. Teams themselves are defined in Workspace settings — see Workspace settings & teams. Everyone in the team is notified when it is given the project, or a new role on it, and when its access is removed.
